modules.module_title: Preparing the metal surface for inlaying

pcs.pc_description: receive the metal product from engraver to be inlayed (usually the product is made of harder metal)
inspect the metal craft and ensure grooves are as per standards to hold the metal string / wire / strip for inlay process
work on the grooves to ensure appropriate setting width / depth by chiseling in them (if required)
clean the surface of the metal before starting the inlaying process

modules.module_title: Inlaying the metal strips / wire into the craft

pcs.pc_description: select the metal to be inlayed in the form of wire / strip / sheet
ensure uniformity of the width of the metal and make sure that it sets into the grooves
ensure the metal strip / sheet meets the design requirement (including colour)
apply glue or bonding agent in the grooves (if applicable)
place the metal wire / strip over the metal craft and hammer them in a way that it sets into grooves
hammer them using appropriate pressure so that it sets into the groove and it does not damage the craft / wire
ensure it sets into the groove firmly
use different type of metal strips as per design requirements at appropriate places
hammer the grooves at edges to close the setting (if applicable)
check the setting once it is complete and its conformity with design specification
achieve the finish as per design parameters and specification
set the metal strips / wire and ensure it does not come out of the craft
complete the craft within the agreed time and quality and meet the targets

pcs.pc_description: Ensure proper composition of zinc and copper metals in the alloy.
Melt the alloy at the appropriate temperature and pour into molds.
Ensure the casting is free of defects such as air bubbles or incomplete forms.
Smooth and refine the base metal surface using filing and sanding techniques.
Accurately transfer the design onto the metal using traditional tools or stencils.
Follow design outlines meticulously, ensuring symmetry and precision.
Use chisels to etch or engrave the design without causing cracks or unwanted marks on the metal surface.
Ensure consistent depth of the etching for better inlaying later.
Cut metal (silver, gold, brass and copper) sheets or wires to match the intricate design patterns.
Embed metal into the etched grooves with precision, ensuring tight fitting without gaps.
Smooth the Metal inlay so it is flush with the surface of the base metal.
Ensure there is no over-spilling or misalignment of the inlay.
Smoothen the inlaid object with files, sandpaper, or buffing tools without damaging the silver or base metal.
Achieve a smooth, shiny finish on the object, ensuring no scratches or rough patches are visible.
Apply the traditional blackening solution (usually a mix of copper sulfate and soil from the Bidar Fort) evenly over the entire object.
Ensure that the blackening agent adheres uniformly without affecting the inlay.
Wipe the surface to reveal the contrast between the darkened base metal and the bright inlay.
Perform any necessary touch-ups to enhance the design, including re-polishing and correcting minor defects.
